ai.description: This 4–5 cm frog is globular with a small head and short limbs. It is grey-brown with dark mottling and a pale belly. Key features include a smooth, thick skin and shovel-shaped metatarsal tubercles.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Uperodon globulosus* is best distinguished by its distinctively globular, bloated body shape and the presence of small, scattered tubercles on its smooth, dark skin.
ai.habitat: The Indian Globular Frog inhabits tropical dry deciduous forests and scrublands, typically found in leaf litter or burrows at elevations below 500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Indian Globular Frog is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending much of its time buried underground and emerging during monsoon rains to forage for termites and ants.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uperodon globulosus* is an explosive breeder that lays thousands of eggs in temporary monsoon pools during the rainy season (June–August).
ai.distributionRemarks: The Indian Globular Frog is found across the Indian subcontinent, primarily inhabiting the plains and low-elevation regions of Northern and Central India.
ai.callDescription: The Indian Globular Frog produces a loud, low-pitched, resonant "whoop" or "hollow" call, typically heard from flooded fields and temporary monsoon pools.
